bull.b: Record revenue, more than $1 billion of new contracts, and a backlog of approximately $2.36 billion provide substantial forward demand visibility. The mix across Launch and Space Systems supports broader revenue durability and gives Rocket Lab a stronger base for scaling operations over the next several quarters.

The improvement in gross margin from earlier periods, together with Q2 performance above guidance, indicates better unit economics as the business scales. Sustained margin progress could strengthen operating leverage and improve the path toward profitability, even though the company remains loss-making today.

Very low leverage and substantial liquidity give Rocket Lab financial flexibility to fund Neutron development, production capacity, and strategic initiatives. The stronger capital structure reduces near-term balance-sheet strain and supports continued investment in programs intended to expand the company’s long-term market position.

bear.b: Rocket Lab continues to consume substantial cash while reporting negative operating and net margins, showing that growth has not yet translated into self-funded operations. Continued investment can support expansion, but prolonged losses and cash burn may require ongoing financing and constrain capital allocation flexibility.

Recent acquisitions add capabilities and potential scale, but the disclosed inventory reserve and initial Mynaric margin pressure show that integration carries execution costs. Until synergies are realized, acquired operations may dilute consolidated profitability and make margins less predictable over the medium term.

Neutron is a major expansion program, but a narrowing launch window and remaining testing milestones create execution uncertainty around when the platform can begin contributing. Delays could extend elevated development spending, postpone anticipated capability expansion, and keep profitability under pressure for longer.
